name: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller: Full
notes: Issue #66: the two-interface USB device a Switch 2 Pro Controller on firmware 1.1.5 presents, for the hosts that read its motion. Interface 0 is HID, with the 97-byte report descriptor the switch2-pro-controller profile carries. Interface 1 is class 0xFF with a bulk pair, where SDL's Switch 2 driver and Steam send the command protocol that starts the pad. The device and configuration descriptors are a real pad's, byte for byte, from the link-layer capture in switch2_controller_research (captures/usb/rumble-procon-gccon.pcapng, frames 44, 71 and 76): USB 2.00, class EF/02/01, bcdDevice 0x0101, full speed, 80 bytes of configuration. No serialString is set, so string 3 is the controller's own synthetic serial and never the 00 a real pad reports. Strings 4, 5 and 6 stall, since no reference records them. The microsoftOs descriptors make Windows bind WinUSB to interface 1 with no driver install, which libusb needs before it can claim the interface: string 0xEE with vendor code 0x01, the code a real pad on later firmware gave Windows, and the compatible ID and DeviceInterfaceGUID tables two device-side emulators serve (switch2-controllers-windows10-gyro usbip_server.py, XinHeLianSheng-Pro2-Bridge usb_switch2_vendor.c). No capture holds a pad's own copy of those two tables. The pad sends nothing until a host sends command 03/0D. From then on it sends one report every 4 ms, 0x09 by default and 0x05 once a host selects it with 03/0A. Report 0x05 carries the accelerometer and gyro while feature 0x04 is enabled. The device side builds every report (sdk/HIDMaestro.Core/Internal/Usbip/Switch2ProDevice.cs), so SubmitState only replaces the state the next one is built from, and the raw submit methods throw. extendedReport declares report 0x09's layout for the report builder, the layout block and stick discovery, field for field what switch2-pro-controller declares. The codec does not send it. Rumble is output report 0x02, decoded to leftMotor and rightMotor on OutputDecoded. Only a host that speaks the bulk protocol gets input: SDL built with libusb, and Steam. DirectInput, RawInput, Windows.Gaming.Input and browsers see a gamepad that never reports, as they do with a real pad on Windows, and switch2-pro-controller remains the profile for them. Not emulated: headset audio, NFC, pairing, firmware update and the magnetometer.
